payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the requested edit—putting a frog in the toilet—fully complete in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass only if the edited image visibly shows the requested frog placed inside the toilet bowl and there is no clear evidence that the requested edit remains incomplete. Fail if the image clearly shows that no frog has been placed inside the toilet bowl, or clearly shows the requested edit is only partially fulfilled. Unknown if the image does not provide enough evidence to determine whether the requested edit is complete. Assess only fulfillment of the requested frog-in-toilet edit; unrelated details do not count as requested progress.
node.binding: Compare the edited image with the source toilet and assess whether the requested frog placement is fully fulfilled. This decision evaluates completion of R1, not merely whether any frog is present somewhere in the image.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image visibly shows a frog inside the open toilet bowl. Additional frogs appear elsewhere, but the requested placement is clearly fulfilled.

response.content: {"text":"The trace’s evidence supports that a frog is inside the bowl, so the node’s current completion criterion reasonably returns yes; it does not explain the reference partial. The edited image also shows frogs on the raised tank area, toilet lid, and floor, but these extra placements do not by themselves make the requested frog-in-toilet edit incomplete. Do not treat multiplicity or unrelated placements as failure without a requirement basis. Investigate whether the binding or criterion is conflating “a frog is inside the bowl” with full fulfillment, and whether the bowl placement is actually clear in the image; compare the source and edit and ground any partial judgment in visible evidence of incomplete placement, not the reference label alone. Preserve unknown for insufficient visual evidence. The trace is valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport or schema failure; its 0.99 confidence merits checking for overconfidence, but is not evidence of an absent edit."}
